item.title: COMING THIS FRIDAY | Songs & Seasons: Wisdom, Humor & Music ft. Linda Mitchell, Mark Goldthwaite & Em Hurley — Sun Oct 18 — Kittredge Arts Center
item.description:
Friday, October 23 | 5 PM – 8 PM | Williams Recital Hall | From $36.22 Event Details and Tickets
Join some of Western North Carolina’s Musical Trailblazers as they share their music, histories and amazing stories at the beautiful Williams Recital Hall @ Kittredge Arts Center on the Campus of Warren Wilson College! Three amazing performers: Wondrous Jazz Veteran Linda Mitchell, Father of the MGB’s and Owner of Asheville Guitar Bar Mark Goldthwaite and Ovadya’s Amazing Singer Songwriter Poet Em Hurley. Free hors d’oeuvres come with entry donation.
Nestled within the beautiful, historic Warren Wilson College campus, the Kittredge Arts Center provides a centralized location for the arts at WWC and WNC. The Center features the 321-seat Kittredge Theater and 80-seat Williams Recital Hall, where concerts and other performance events are featured throughout the year.

item.title: Strawberry Gap and Trombatore trails, 10 mile Fitness Hike. — Wed Oct 21, 9:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **This will be a strenuous out and back hike of about 10.1 miles and 2,400 feet of elevation gain ( level 8\*) as we hike up the Eastern Contential Divide**. We will pass through thick rhododendrons and mountain laurels, pass large boulders and experience long-range views at Ferguson Peak and the Blue Ridge Pasture, and continue with a forest hike on the Trombatore Trail. We begin with a steep climb on the well-maintained Strawberry Gap trail. At \~2.5 miles, we will enter the open Blue Ridge Pastures for long range views and connect to the Trombatore forest trail. We will turn around at the end of the Trombatore Trail after a snack/water break.
**PACE**: This hike will be at a brisk pace (between 2.5-3 mi/hr) adjusting for steepness of grade and/or rugged trail conditions, brief regrouping as needed. This 10 mile level 8 fitness oriented hike of 2400 feet gain is for conditioned hikers. Join us If you like fitness oriented hike workouts.

item.title: Beginning Botany — Fri Nov 20, 1:00 PM
item.description: Beginning Botany with Alexandra Holland Friday, November 20 | 1 – 4pm BRN and BREG Core Register Here! It’s a tough life for a plant: make dinner, create and nurture offspring, fight off predators, deal with the neighbors. In Beginning Botany we’ll explore how plants handle these daily challenges using and modifying only leaves, stems, and roots. We’ll cover the basics of plant structure and function. Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography. She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin. While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center. item.title: Mammals of the Southern Appalachians — Sat Nov 21, 12:00 PM
item.description: Mammals of the Southern Appalachians with Carlton Burke Saturday, November 21 | 12 – 4pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here! The rugged mountains of Appalachia host a tremendous variety of mammal species ranging from tiny shrews weighing only a few ounces at most to huge mammals such as the black bear which can weigh in at several hundred pounds. Also large mammals such as the cougar, bison, and elk also once commonly roamed these mountains. In this class we will discuss present and past mammals of the region, their distribution, natural life cycles, and also controversies and cultural connections they have with the ever increasing human population of the area. Class participants will also have a chance to meet a few live, native mammal species of the mountain region as well. item.title: Vaden Landers — Sat Dec 5, 8:30 PM
item.description:
Vaden Landers is a multi-instumentalist & singer-songwriter hailing from eastern Tennessee who blends influences from honky tonk, hillbilly, folk, blues, ragtime, jazz, western swing and old-time Appalachian to bring new fire to a classic sound!
As a teen, he set out traveling the American highways & railways, learning the ways of a traveler-musician while honing his songwriting, singing, yodeling & picking skills busking & touring from Alaska to Florida.
Landers' original songs harken back to the golden days of country music and, with a voice that draws comparison to Hank Sr., he continues to turn heads as an exciting new player in the revival of the traditional country music scene.
Music from 8:30-11:30, $10 cover at the door.

Get Help | The Storehouse of Henderson County https://storehouseonline.org/get-help
What to Expect & Bring
Eligibility: Assistance is available to residents of Henderson County facing food insecurity.
What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).
No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.
The Process: Volunteers will greet you, help you with a brief registration, and provide you with a selection of fresh and non-perishable food items.
